db_evidence.notes: The correct episode window (337800-338952, 30sec granularity) is present in the DB and its captions describe near-continuous feeding, chopstick/hand eating, and skewer-biting across virtually every 30s segment of the 927s interval, confirming the true bite count plausibly reaches 18. However, episode captions are qualitative scene summaries, not per-bite counts -- getting to 18 requires exhaustive frame-by-frame visual counting over the full interval, which none of the 5 rollouts achieved: three (0, 2, 3) passed clip_qa incomplete/gappy time windows, one (1) retrieved an entirely wrong Changsha table-eating episode (~326500-326950, a spicy fish/crawfish meal) that only superficially matches the query semantically, and the one rollout (4) that passed the full correct window still undercounted because its clip_qa sub-agent's own frame-sampling budget (~1000 images) forced sparse initial sampling plus only partial dense zoom-ins, leaving large sub-windows (including the final ~150s) without fine-grained coverage.

root_causes: Genuinely hard long-horizon counting question: 18 bites spread across a continuous 927s (~15.5 min) eating scene requires dense, exhaustive frame sampling that no rollout fully performed.

One rollout (1) retrieved the wrong episode entirely -- a semantically similar but distinct Changsha table-eating scene ~11500s away from the true window -- because semantic search on 'dining table food bites' matched multiple Changsha meal scenes and the agent didn't verify the 'ancient city' qualifier before committing to a window.

Three rollouts (0, 2, 3) located the correct episode but issued clip_qa calls covering only a fraction of the 927s interval (fragmented with gaps, or truncated before the end), guaranteeing an undercount regardless of visual-agent accuracy.

Even the one rollout (4) that requested the full correct interval was limited by the clip_qa sub-agent's own image/frame budget (~1000 frames): a sparse 0.1fps pass over 900s followed by dense zoom-ins on only a subset of flagged sub-windows left large stretches (including the final ~150s) without fine-grained coverage, so bites there went uncounted.

No rollout used a systematic tiling strategy (e.g. several equal-length dense clip_qa sub-calls covering the whole interval end-to-end with counts summed) that would guarantee full coverage within any single sub-agent's per-call frame budget.
what_worked: 4 of 5 rollouts (0, 2, 3, 4) correctly used semantic_search plus run_sql on episodes to locate the true ancient-city dining-table scene at 337800-338952.
Rollout 2's self-correction: after an initial wrong-window exploration (326400-326900, same trap as rollout 1), it queried the correct window before answering.
Rollout 4's clip_qa call is the closest structurally to what would be needed -- it passed the entire correct interval to the visual sub-agent -- but was still capped by the sub-agent's frame budget.
transferable_lessons: For long-horizon fine-grained counting questions (e.g. bites, taps, steps) spanning many minutes, a single clip_qa call over the whole interval is insufficient even if given the right window -- the visual sub-agent has a finite frame budget and will sparse-sample or leave gaps; instead tile the interval into several shorter clip_qa calls (e.g. 60-120s each) that together cover it end-to-end, and sum the per-window counts.

When semantic_search on episodes surfaces multiple candidate scenes that share surface features (e.g. 'Changsha', 'table', 'eating'), explicitly cross-check distinguishing qualifiers from the question (here: 'ancient city', 'big dining table' vs a street-food stall) against the episode text before committing to a time window -- don't anchor on the first or highest-ranked match.

Before calling clip_qa, use the episodes table's own captions to gauge how much eating/action activity is described across the full clue window; if captions show continuous activity throughout, that's a signal a single narrow or gapped visual sample will undercount.

For counting questions with 'Long' temporal certificate, treat full-interval coverage as a hard requirement to check before submit_answer: verify (e.g. by listing clip_qa windows called) that they union to the full total_intervals span with no gaps, not just that one clip_qa call was made.
open_questions: Whether the judge's rubric would have scored any answer other than exactly 18 (or very close) as non-zero -- rollout 4's 11 was the closest but still scored 0, suggesting a strict/near-exact-match counting rubric; not independently confirmed since judge segment reasoning wasn't inspected.

The reference answer of 18 bites was not independently reproduced by frame-by-frame manual counting in this diagnosis (only inferred plausible from episode captions describing continuous eating); it's possible the reference count itself depends on a specific bite definition (e.g. including hand-fed morsels, chewing continuations) that no rollout matched.
